extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and researchers interested in journalism, media ethics, and notable journalistic scandals
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography summarizing Janet Cooke's career, the fabrication of her story "Jimmy's World," the discovery and investigation of that fabrication, and the professional and public consequences. Useful as a case study of journalistic verification, editorial responsibility, and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness / Accuracy of reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooke's September 28, 1980 article 'Jimmy's World' was later discovered to have been fabricated; she admitted she had fabricated stories and returned the Pulitzer Prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabrication of reporting invalidates journalistic work, can lead to returning awards (the prize was returned and re-awarded to Teresa Carpenter), public censure, and career-ending consequences. Example: 'she publicly confessed this and announced her resignation from the Post.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of notes and recorded interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors reviewed her notes and recorded interviews for the story and 'found no evidence that she had ever interviewed a child who was using heroin.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and review contemporaneous notes/recordings as primary evidence; absence of supporting documentation is a key indicator that reporting may be fabricated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration of sources, especially anonymous ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal questions were raised that the story 'not sounding right, being based on anonymous sources.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories relying heavily on anonymous sources or containing extraordinary claims require stronger corroboration and editorial scrutiny to guard against fabrication or error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight and responsibility in publishing and prize nomination
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistant managing editor Bob Woodward submitted the story for the Pulitzer Prize; later reflection noted differing views about an editor's duty to verify authenticity of nominated stories ('It would be absurd for me or any other editor to review the authenticity or accuracy of stories that are nominated for prizes.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are responsible for vetting significant or prize-nominated pieces; failure to adequately investigate can result in reputational damage and revoked honors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of a journalist's background and credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: An Associated Press article about Pulitzer winners featured Cooke's biographical profile; the Toledo Blade noticed discrepancies in her reported educational background and alerted the AP and the Post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic employers and awarding bodies should verify claimed education, prior awards, language abilities, and other résumé claims (example: Bradlee tested her language abilities and found they were exaggerated). Cross-check with previous employers and records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing claimed practical skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive editor Ben Bradlee later tested her language abilities, and found that she spoke no Portuguese or Italian and only rudimentary French.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When journalists claim specialized skills (language fluency, technical expertise), practical testing or verification can prevent misrepresentation and ensure competence for assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public impact and potential harm from fabricated stories
rubrics_metrics.description: The article 'sparked immediate and extraordinary public outcry' and city officials (including the mayor) organized a police search for the alleged child, which was unsuccessful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabricated reporting can waste public resources, cause unnecessary public alarm, and harm individuals; reporters and editors must consider the consequences of publishing unverified human-interest claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational culture and pressure as a risk factor for unethical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooke appeared on The Phil Donahue Show and said that 'the high-pressure environment of the Post had corrupted her judgment' and that she created a story to satisfy her editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-pressure newsroom expectations and competitiveness can incentivize fabrication; news organizations should monitor culture, workloads, and incentives to reduce ethical lapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability mechanisms and remedial actions after discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: After discrepancies were revealed, Cooke admitted fabrication, resigned, and returned the Pulitzer Prize; the prize was instead given to the original nominee, Teresa Carpenter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When fabrication is discovered, remedial steps include public confession/retraction, resignation or employment action, returning or revoking awards, and reassigning honors to rightful recipients to restore integrity.
